title: OpenCode HTTP Message Shape Probe
summary: The FP-MCP-249 OpenCode HTTP message response shape probe ran with cleanup enabled. It created one titled OpenCode session, submitted the tiny canary prompt through /session/{id}/prompt_async, polled /session/{id}/message, returned structural message shapes and bounded text excerpts, and deleted only the created canary session. The probe returned sessionCreated=true, promptAsyncSubmitted=true, promptAsyncHttpStatus=204, messagesHttpStatus=200, messagesTopLevelType=array, messagesCount=2, canaryTextObserved=true, discoveredTextPaths=["[0].parts[0].text"], boundedTextExcerpts=["Return exactly: OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK"], sessionDeleted=true, and deleteHttpStatus=200. The observed message array contained entry 0 with keys info and parts, info.role=user, and parts[0] keys id,messageID,sessionID,text,type. Entry 1 had keys info and parts, info.role=assistant, but partsLength=0 at capture time. This explains the FP-MCP-248 observation where one assistant message existed but assistant text was not extractable: assistant metadata may appear before assistant text parts are populated, and user prompt text can satisfy naive canary text detection unless role-aware filtering is used.
caveats: The probe observed the canary text in the user message path [0].parts[0].text, not in assistant output.
Assistant message metadata existed as the second array entry, but partsLength was 0 at capture time.
The current shape probe stopped as soon as any canary text was observed, so it may have stopped before assistant text populated.
Completion readers must be role-aware and should require assistant-role text parts, not merely presence of the canary string anywhere in messages.
No wait endpoint was called in this probe.
